records.source: כִּֽי־תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what [is] before you,
pieces: When you are seated at a ruler's table, \q take careful note of what is in front of you,

L.1: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, \q consider carefully what [is] before you,

R.1: Suppose you are invited to eat with an important ruler. \q Pay close attention to what is set before you.

decisions.choice: what is before you: the food, or the host
decisions.reason: The words can mean the dishes set out or the powerful person across the table. Either way the guest must stay alert; verses 1–3 are one piece of advice. They belong to "the words of the wise" (22:17–24:22), a collection with close parallels in the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, which also warns about eating in the presence of a great man.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: and you will put a knife in your throat if [are] a master of appetite you.
pieces: and if you have a big appetite, \q hold a knife to your own throat.

L.2: and put a knife to your throat \q if you [are] a person of [great] appetite.

R.2: If you love to eat, hold yourself back, \q as if a knife were at your throat.

decisions.choice: a knife to your throat: restrain yourself sternly
decisions.reason: The picture is an overstatement: treat your own greed as an enemy to be stopped. The throat is the place of appetite (nephesh, in the next words, can mean both).

records.source: אַל־תִּ֭תְאָולְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: Do not crave for his delicacies, and it [is] food of lies.
pieces: Do not long for the ruler's fine dishes, \q for that food is deceptive.

L.3: Do not crave {{gender:their|his}} delicacies, \q for it [is] food of lies.

R.3: Do not be greedy for his fancy food. \q It is not what it seems.

decisions.choice: food of lies: a meal with a hidden purpose
decisions.reason: The rich meal may be meant to win the guest over or to test him. Its generosity is not to be trusted.

records.source: אַל־תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃
records.gloss: Do not labor to gain riches; from your understanding cease.
pieces: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; \q have the sense to stop.

L.4: Do not wear yourself out to gain riches; \q cease from your [own] understanding.

R.4: Do not work yourself to death trying to get rich. \q Be wise enough to stop.

decisions.choice: cease from your understanding: stop, using good sense
alternatives: stop relying on your own cleverness
decisions.reason: The line may mean "in your wisdom, stop" or "stop trusting your own schemes for getting rich" (3:5, 7). Both warn against making wealth the goal of life.

decisions.choice: do not toil for riches: a teaching shared with Amenemope
decisions.reason: The Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope has a close parallel to verses 4–5, including riches that fly away like birds.

records.source: הֲתָ֤עִיף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָע֥וּף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: Do you cause to fly your eyes on it, and it [is] not? For surely it makes for itself wings like an eagle [that] flies [to] the heavens.
pieces: Cast a glance at wealth, and it is gone; \q it grows wings \q and flies off to the sky like an eagle.

L.5: Will you let your eyes fly to it, and it [is] gone? \q For it surely makes itself wings \q like an eagle [that] flies [toward] the sky.

R.5: Money can disappear in the blink of an eye. \q It is like a bird that grows wings and flies away.

decisions.choice: will you let your eyes fly, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: will your eyes fly (the written form)
decisions.reason: The two forms differ only in the verb's stem; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: flies, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: let your eyes fly to it, and it is gone: wealth vanishes in a glance
decisions.reason: The eyes fly to wealth, and wealth flies away. The bird (nesher) may be an eagle or a vulture.

records.source: אַל־תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Do not eat the food of [one] evil of eye, and do not crave for his delicacies,
pieces: Do not eat at the table of a stingy host, \q and do not long for their fine food,

L.6: Do not eat the food of [one with an] evil eye, \q and do not crave {{gender:their|his}} delicacies,

R.6: Do not eat at the table of a stingy person. \q Do not want their fancy food.

decisions.choice: evil of eye: stingy, grudging
decisions.reason: The "evil eye" is the opposite of the "good eye" of 22:9, the generous person (28:22).

decisions.choice: crave, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

records.source: כִּ֤י׀כְּמוֹ־שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For as he calculates in his soul, so [is] he. Eat and drink, he says to you, but his heart [is] not with you.
pieces: Such people are always counting the cost. \q "Eat and drink!" they say to you, \q but their heart is not with you.

L.7: For as {{gender:they|he}} reckons within {{gender:themselves|himself}}, so [is] {{gender:that one|he}}. \q "Eat and drink," {{gender:they say|he says}} to you, \q but {{gender:their|his}} heart [is] not with you.

R.7: That kind of person keeps track of every bite you take. \q They tell you, "Eat and drink!" \q But they do not mean it.

decisions.choice: as he reckons within himself: he counts the cost
alternatives: as he thinks in his heart, so is he
like a hair in the throat
decisions.reason: The verb (shaar) occurs only here; a related word means a measure or price. The host calculates what the meal costs him. The ancient Greek translation reads the line differently, with a picture of someone swallowing a hair. The familiar saying "as he thinks in his heart, so is he" takes the line out of its setting.

decisions.choice: always counting the cost; keeps track of every bite
alternatives: as he reckons within himself, so is he
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the rare verb plainly.

records.source: פִּֽתְּךָ־אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃
records.gloss: Your morsel [which] you have eaten you will vomit it up, and you will waste your pleasant words.
pieces: You will throw up the little you have eaten \q and squander your gracious words.

L.8: The morsel you have eaten you will vomit up, \q and you will waste your pleasant words.

R.8: You will feel sick about what you ate. \q All your polite thanks will be wasted.

decisions.choice: vomit up ... waste your pleasant words: the meal turns sour
decisions.reason: Once the guest sees the host's real attitude, the food sickens him and his compliments were for nothing.

records.source: בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: In [the] ears of a fool do not speak, for he will despise the insight of your words.
pieces: Do not talk to a fool, \q who will only scorn your wise words.

L.9: Do not speak in [the] ears of a fool, \q for {{gender:they|he}} will despise the good sense of your words.

R.9: Do not waste your breath on a fool. \q A fool will laugh at your good advice.

decisions.choice: fool: the closed-minded fool (kesil)
decisions.reason: Compare 9:7–8 and 26:4; Matthew 7:6.

records.source: אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־תָּבֹֽא׃
records.gloss: Do not displace a boundary of antiquity, and into [the] fields of fatherless ones do not go,
pieces: Do not shift an ancient boundary marker \q or encroach on the fields of orphans,

L.10: Do not move an ancient boundary stone, \q and do not go into [the] fields of [the] fatherless,

R.10: Do not move the old stones that mark where a field ends. \q Do not take land that belongs to orphans.

decisions.choice: an ancient boundary: the stones marking a family's land
decisions.reason: Fields were marked by boundary stones, and moving them was theft (22:28; Deuteronomy 19:14; 27:17). The Instruction of Amenemope also forbids moving boundary markers and taking a widow's land.

decisions.choice: the fatherless: those with no one to defend their land
decisions.reason: Orphans and widows were easy targets because they had no man to defend them in court (15:25).

records.source: כִּֽי־גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: for their redeemer [is] strong; he will conduct their case against you.
pieces: for their Defender is strong, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will argue their cause against you.

L.11: for their Redeemer [is] strong; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will plead their case against you.

R.11: God is their protector, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is strong. \q He will take their side against you.

decisions.choice: their Redeemer: God as the next of kin of the helpless
decisions.reason: The redeemer (goel) was the relative who bought back family land and defended its people (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4). The fatherless have no such relative, so the LORD takes the role himself (22:23; Jeremiah 50:34).

decisions.choice: Defender
decisions.reason: Balanced names the role the verse describes: one who takes up their case.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the Redeemer stands for here, as the verse sense requires (22:23).

records.source: הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Bring to discipline your heart, and your ear to words of knowledge.
pieces: Set your mind on instruction \q and your ears on words of knowledge.

L.12: Bring your heart to discipline, \q and your ear to words of knowledge.

R.12: Pay attention when you are taught. \q Listen carefully to wise words.

decisions.choice: bring your heart to discipline: a new call to listen
decisions.reason: Like 22:17, the verse opens a fresh section of the teacher's words.

records.source: אַל־תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: Do not withhold from a youth discipline; if you strike him with the rod, he will not die.
pieces: Do not hold back correction from a child; \q if you punish them with the rod, they will not die.

L.13: Do not withhold discipline from a child; \q if you strike {{gender:them|him}} with the rod, {{gender:they|he}} will not die.

R.13: Do not be afraid to correct a child. \q Punishing them with the rod will not kill them.

decisions.choice: the rod: physical discipline
decisions.reason: The rod was the usual means of correcting a child in the ancient world (13:24; 22:15; 29:15). The point of the saying is that love corrects; the means belongs to its time and must be read in the light of all Scripture says about love and justice.

decisions.choice: he will not die: correction will not destroy him
alternatives: he will not die an early death
decisions.reason: The line answers a parent's fear that correction is too harsh. Verse 14 adds that discipline keeps the child from a worse death.

records.source: אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: You with the rod you will strike him, and his life from Sheol you will deliver.
pieces: Punish them with the rod yourself, \q and you will save their life from Sheol.

L.14: You, strike {{gender:them|him}} with the rod, \q and you will deliver {{gender:their|his}} life from Sheol.

R.14: When you correct them, \q you are saving them from an early grave.

decisions.choice: you ... from Sheol: correction saves from death
decisions.reason: The "you" is emphatic: the parent who corrects is the one who rescues. Sheol is the world of the dead; a life without correction ends there early (5:23; 19:18).

records.source: בְּ֭נִי אִם־חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: My son, if is wise your heart, will rejoice my heart, even I.
pieces: My son, if you have a wise heart, \q then I myself will be glad at heart.

L.15: My son, if your heart is wise, \q my heart will rejoice, even mine.

R.15: My son, if you become wise, \q I will be very happy.

decisions.choice: even I: the father's own joy
decisions.reason: The added "I" stresses that the teacher himself is moved (10:1; 27:11).

records.source: וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And my kidneys will rejoice when your lips speak upright [things].
pieces: I will be glad to the depths of my being \q when I hear you speak what is right.

L.16: And my inmost being will exult \q when your lips speak what is right.

R.16: I will be full of joy when I hear you say what is right.

decisions.choice: my kidneys: my inmost self
decisions.reason: The kidneys stood for the deepest feelings (Psalm 16:7; Jeremiah 12:2).

records.source: אַל־יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־בְּיִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Do not let your heart be jealous of sinners, but [be] in the fear of YHWH all the day.
pieces: Do not let your heart envy sinners; \q instead, live in the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all day long.

L.17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, \q but [continue] in the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the day.

R.17: Do not be jealous of people who do wrong. \q Instead, always honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe.

decisions.choice: but in the fear of the LORD: the verb is understood
decisions.reason: The second line has no verb; "be" or "continue" is implied (24:1, 19; Psalm 37:1).

records.source: כִּ֭י אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃
records.gloss: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
pieces: Surely there is a future for you, \q and your hope will not be cut off.

L.18: For surely there is a future, \q and your hope will not be cut off.

R.18: You really do have a future. \q What you hope for will happen.

decisions.choice: a future: a good outcome at the end
decisions.reason: The word (aharit) is the end or outcome of a life (24:14, 20). Sinners may prosper now, but the one who fears the LORD has the better end.

records.source: שְׁמַע־אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Listen, you, my son, and be wise, and guide in the way your heart.
pieces: Listen, my son, and become wise; \q set your heart straight on the way.

L.19: Listen, you, my son, and be wise, \q and direct your heart in the way.

R.19: Listen, my son, and be wise. \q Keep your mind on the right way to live.

decisions.choice: direct your heart in the way: keep to the right path
decisions.reason: The verb (ishsher) means to go straight ahead (4:14; 9:6). "The way" is the way of wisdom.

records.source: אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: Do not be among drinkers of wine, among gluttons of meat for themselves,
pieces: Do not keep company with heavy drinkers of wine \q or with those who stuff themselves with meat,

L.20: Do not be among drinkers of wine, \q among those who gorge themselves on meat,

R.20: Do not spend time with people who drink too much or eat too much.

decisions.choice: drunkard and glutton: the rebellious son of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The same pair describes the son who will not listen to his parents (Deuteronomy 21:20).

records.source: כִּי־סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃
records.gloss: For a drunkard and a glutton will become poor, and drowsiness will clothe [in] rags.
pieces: For drunkards and gluttons will end up poor, \q and their drowsiness will dress them in rags.

L.21: For [the] drunkard and [the] glutton will become poor, \q and drowsiness will clothe [them in] rags.

R.21: People who drink and eat too much will become poor. \q They get lazy and end up in rags.

decisions.choice: drowsiness: the sleepiness that follows feasting
decisions.reason: The dullness after too much food and drink leads to laziness and so to poverty (6:9–11).

records.source: שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Listen to your father who begot you, and do not despise when she is old your mother.
pieces: Listen to the father who gave you life, \q and do not look down on your mother when she is old.

L.22: Listen to your father who gave you life, \q and do not despise your mother when she is old.

R.22: Listen to your father, who gave you life. \q Do not look down on your mother when she grows old.

decisions.choice: honor father and mother: as in the commandment
decisions.reason: Compare Exodus 20:12; Proverbs 1:8; 19:26; 30:17.

records.source: אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃
records.gloss: Truth buy and do not sell, wisdom and discipline and understanding.
pieces: Buy the truth and never sell it; \q get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.

L.23: Buy truth and do not sell [it]; \q [buy] wisdom and discipline and understanding.

R.23: Truth is worth paying for, so get it and never give it up. \q Do the same with wisdom, correction, and understanding.

decisions.choice: buy ... do not sell: gain at any cost and never give up
decisions.reason: As in 4:5, 7, wisdom is something to acquire like a valuable possession.

records.source: גִּ֣יל יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם יִשְׂמַח־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Greatly rejoices [the] father of a righteous [son], and [one who] begets a wise [son] he rejoices in him.
pieces: The father of a righteous son will be full of joy; \q a man who has a wise son will delight in him.

L.24: [The] father of a righteous [son] will greatly rejoice, \q and [one who] fathers a wise [son] will be glad in him.

R.24: A father is very happy when his son does what is right. \q He is proud when his son is wise.

decisions.choice: greatly rejoices ... and one who fathers ... will be glad, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: the written form, spelled differently and without "and"
decisions.reason: The scribes' reading differs in the spelling of the verbs and adds "and" before the second line. The sense is the same.

records.source: יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: May your father and your mother rejoice, and may she rejoice, the [one who] bore you.
pieces: Let your father and mother be glad; \q let her who gave birth to you rejoice.

L.25: May your father and your mother be glad, \q and may she who bore you rejoice.

R.25: So make your father and mother happy. \q Bring joy to the mother who gave birth to you.

decisions.choice: may they rejoice: a wish that is also a call to the son
decisions.reason: The son can bring this joy about by living wisely (verse 24; 10:1).

records.source: תְּנָֽה־בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תִּצֹּֽרְנָה׃
records.gloss: Give, my son, your heart to me, and your eyes my ways let them observe.
pieces: Give me your heart, my son, \q and let your eyes watch my ways.

L.26: My son, give me your heart, \q and let your eyes observe my ways.

R.26: My son, pay attention to me. \q Watch how I live and follow my example.

decisions.choice: let your eyes observe, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: let your eyes delight in (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written form has a different verb: "let your eyes take pleasure in my ways."

decisions.choice: give me your heart: the father speaks, warning of the prostitute
decisions.reason: The appeal leads into the warning of verses 27–28, as in chapters 5–7.

records.source: כִּֽי־שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: For a deep pit [is] a prostitute, and a narrow well [is] a foreign [woman].
pieces: A prostitute is a deep pit; \q a foreign woman is a narrow well.

L.27: For a prostitute [is] a deep pit, \q and a foreign woman [is] a narrow well.

R.27: A prostitute is like a deep pit you fall into. \q A woman who belongs to another man is like a narrow well you cannot climb out of.

decisions.choice: a prostitute ... a foreign woman: the woman of chapters 5–7
decisions.reason: The foreign woman (nokhriyyah) is the woman outside one's marriage (2:16; 5:20; 7:5). A pit and a narrow well are traps with no way out (22:14).

decisions.choice: a woman who belongs to another man
decisions.reason: Readable explains whom the foreign woman stands for, as in chapter 7.

records.source: אַף־הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃
records.gloss: Also she like a robber lies in wait, and the treacherous among humankind she increases.
pieces: She lies in wait like a robber \q and makes many men unfaithful.

L.28: She also lies in wait like a robber, \q and increases the treacherous among people.

R.28: She waits to catch men, like a robber. \q Because of her, many men break their promises to their wives.

decisions.choice: increases the treacherous: she makes men unfaithful
decisions.reason: Those she catches betray their wives and their vows (2:17). The word for robber (hetef) occurs only here.

records.source: לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י מִדְיָנִ֨ים׀לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: To whom [is] woe? To whom [is] sorrow? To whom [are] contentions? To whom [is] complaint? To whom [are] bruises without cause? To whom [is] dullness of eyes?
pieces: Who has trouble? Who has misery? Who is always fighting? Who is always complaining? \q Who has bruises for no reason? \q Who has bloodshot eyes?

L.29: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaining? \q Who has wounds without cause? \q Who has dullness of eyes?

R.29: Who is in trouble? Who is miserable? Who is always fighting and complaining? \q Who gets hurt for no reason? \q Whose eyes are red and blurry?

decisions.choice: who has woe: a riddle that opens a poem on drunkenness
decisions.reason: Verses 29–35 form one poem. Six questions are answered in verse 30; the teacher then speaks to the listener, and the poem ends in the drinker's own words.

decisions.choice: quarrels, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: dullness of eyes: eyes dull or red from wine
decisions.reason: The word (hakhlilut) occurs only here; a related word is used of eyes darkened with wine in Genesis 49:12.

records.source: לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: To those who delay over the wine, to those who go to examine mixed wine.
pieces: Those who stay up late over wine, \q who go looking for spiced drinks.

L.30: Those who linger over the wine, \q those who go to taste mixed wine.

R.30: It is people who drink wine late into the night. \q They keep trying different kinds of strong drink.

decisions.choice: mixed wine: wine blended with spices
decisions.reason: Wine was mixed with spices or herbs to make it stronger and richer (9:2; Isaiah 5:22).

records.source: אַל־תֵּ֥רֶא יַיִן֮ כִּ֪י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן בַּכּ֣וֹס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Do not look [at] wine when it is red, when it gives in the cup its eye, [when] it goes with smoothness.
pieces: Do not gaze at the red wine \q as it gleams in the cup \q and slides down so easily.

L.31: Do not look [at] wine when it is red, \q when it gives its sparkle in the cup, \q [when] it goes down smoothly.

R.31: Do not stare at red wine sparkling in a cup. \q It goes down easily.

decisions.choice: in the cup, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form can be read as "bag" or "purse"; the scribes' reading has "cup".

decisions.choice: gives its eye: sparkles, shows its gleam
decisions.reason: The "eye" of the wine is its glint or color in the cup.

decisions.choice: goes down smoothly
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of wine in Song of Songs 7:9.

records.source: אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Its end like a snake it will bite, and like a viper it will sting.
pieces: But at the last it bites like a snake \q and strikes like a viper.

L.32: At its end it bites like a snake \q and stings like a viper.

R.32: But later it hurts you like the bite of a poisonous snake.

decisions.choice: viper: a poisonous snake
decisions.reason: The exact kind of snake (tsiphoni) is unknown (Isaiah 11:8). The verse turns from the pleasant start to the painful end (5:4).

records.source: עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Your eyes will see strange [things], and your heart will speak perverse things.
pieces: Your eyes will see strange sights, \q and your mind will say confused and twisted things.

L.33: Your eyes will see strange [things], \q and your heart will utter twisted things.

R.33: You will see things that are not there. \q You will say things that make no sense.

decisions.choice: strange things
decisions.reason: The word (zarot) is feminine plural and could mean "strange women", linking the poem to verses 27–28. More likely it refers to the drinker's confused sight.

records.source: וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃
records.gloss: And you will be like [one who] lies down in [the] heart of [the] sea, and like [one who] lies down at [the] top of a mast.
pieces: You will be like someone sleeping in the middle of the sea, \q like someone lying at the top of a ship's mast.

L.34: And you will be like [one who] lies down in [the] heart of [the] sea, \q like [one who] lies down on [the] top of a mast.

R.34: You will feel dizzy, as if you were lying down on a ship far out at sea, \q or at the top of its tall pole.

decisions.choice: the top of a mast: tossed and swaying
decisions.reason: The word (hibbel) occurs only here; it is related to the word for a sailor or ship's rope. The picture is the drunk's reeling head and his foolish ease in danger.

records.source: הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: They struck me, not I am sick; they beat me, not I know. When will I awake? I will repeat [it]; I will seek it again.
pieces: "They hit me," you will say, "but I was not hurt; \q they beat me, but I did not feel it. \q When will I wake up? \q I will go and look for another drink."

L.35: [You will say,] "They struck me, [but] I was not hurt; \q they beat me, [but] I did not know [it]. \q When will I wake up? \q I will do it again; I will seek it once more."

R.35: You will say, "Someone hit me, but it did not hurt. \q They beat me, but I did not feel a thing. \q When will I wake up? I want another drink!"

decisions.choice: they struck me ... I will seek it again: the drinker speaks
decisions.reason: The poem ends in the drinker's own words. He does not feel the blows, and his first thought on waking is to drink again: wine has made him its slave.

decisions.choice: you will say
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves into the drinker's speech without a verb of saying; it is supplied to mark the quotation.

decisions.choice: another drink
alternatives: I will do it again; I will seek it once more
decisions.reason: "It" is the wine; Balanced and Readable say so.
